items.recapEn: On July 4 the walk resumed at Hiratsuka's Tanabata festival under huge red, blue and yellow streamers. A boy, Yūta, handed Hana a yellow strip; she wrote 'I will reach Kyoto'. She chatted with his grandmother Ishii-san. Tanaka-san appeared at six and predicted rain; the night was clear and quiet, and he asked what time they leave tomorrow.

items.recapEn: In the Hiratsuka arcade Hana practised small talk with Yūta's grandmother Ishii-san: the heat, the huge long streamers, the red one made by Yūta's school. She told them her wish, said she walks with Ken, showed her white hat, and promised to come back around seven to see the streamers at night.

items.recapEn: Hana copied the wish strips into her diary: Yūta's black camera, Ishii-san's wish for a healthy grandson, Ken's 'a kitchen, my own', her own 'I will reach Kyoto', a student's Kyoto school, a man's seven o'clock homecoming, and Tanaka-san's two words, 'To Kyoto'. Five colours of paper, her yellow strip among them.
